title: Goose Animation Version 2
eyebrow: Design for approval · your notes on pull request #7 · nothing built yet

short.lead: You checked the 13 goose clips in pull request #7 (Animate the goose boss: 59-bone rig and 13 clips) and asked for five changes. Everything should be slower and more laboured. Death should fall forward with the heads flat and tongues out. The phase transition should be longer and grander. The stagger should become a knock-down with a stun window, and hits should get their own reactions with several variants. You also asked that the current clips stay as they are, so the new ones can be compared with them. Six choices below settle the details.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: Version 1: 13 clips in art/goose/goose_animated.blend and art/goose/goose_anims.fbx, with videos and sheets in art/goose/clips/. Lengths run from 1.2 s (stagger) to 6 s (The Crown Wakes). The tongues on the heads are fixed to the jaw bone, so they cannot move on their own. The clip script (art/goose/goose_clips.py) already builds every clip from named poses, so a global slow-down and new clips extend it rather than replace it.
How much slower the clips run; how version 1 is kept for comparison; how the tongues hang out in death; how long the phase transition runs; how the stun is split into clips; how many hit variants.
Pick an option for each question under Choices, or write your own.

Every clip is rebuilt slower and heavier: longer wind-ups, visible effort in the strike, and a laboured recovery with heaving breath. Death falls forward. The Crown Wakes becomes a longer set piece. The stagger is replaced by a knock-down stun and a set of hit reactions.
For every clip that exists in both versions, a video with version 1 on the left and version 2 on the right, so you can judge the change directly.
Version 2 goes onto pull request #7 beside version 1, which stays untouched.
You watch the side-by-side videos, then pass or fail version 2.

changes: keep
Version 1 clips
Untouched: goose_animated.blend, goose_anims.fbx and everything in art/goose/clips/.
Nothing in version 1 is rebuilt or overwritten.
new
Version 2 files
goose_animated_v2.blend, goose_anims_v2.fbx and art/goose/clips_v2/, with their own manifest.
Built by the same goose_clips.py with a version switch, so both versions can be rebuilt from the same script.
chg
Death
Falls forward instead of rolling onto its side.
Rolls onto its left side; the heads land at different heights
Collapses forward onto its chest; all three necks stretch out flat in front, jaws slack, tongues out
The end pose holds still, and no part of the goose goes below the floor.
chg
Stagger
Replaced by a knock-down stun and separate hit reactions.
One 1.2 s stagger used for every hit
A knock-down with a stun window to punish, plus several short hit reactions the game picks between at random
Version 1's stagger clip stays in version 1 for comparison.
choices: How much slower should everything be?
1.4 times as long, with effort added

Every clip 40% longer (the script sets this length exactly), plus a heavier feel: deeper wind-ups, a shudder of strain at the strike, the body sagging after it, and heaving breath in the recovery. The peck goes from 2.2 s to 3.1 s.
1.25 times as long, with effort added
A lighter slow-down with the same added effort.
1.6 times as long, with effort added
The slowest; strongest sense of weight, but long attacks give the player more time.
Option A makes the goose read as old and heavy, without stretching its attacks so far that they stop being a threat.
How should version 1 be kept for comparison?
Separate version 2 files plus side-by-side videos
Version 1 stays as it is, version 2 gets its own files, and each shared clip gets a video with version 1 on the left and version 2 on the right.
No side-by-side videos; you compare the two sets yourself.
You asked to compare before and after, and the side-by-side video puts both in one view.
How do the tongues hang out in death?
Three new bones per tongue, so the tongues can loll out over the beak and hang onto the floor. The rig goes from 59 to 68 bones; the mesh does not change.
The jaws fall slack and open wide, but each tongue stays where it was built, inside the mouth, so it shows only through the open jaw.
Today each tongue is fixed rigidly to its jaw, so without new bones it cannot hang out the way you described.
How long and how grand should The Crown Wakes be?

It collapses as if dead, then twitches; the side heads rise one at a time; the crowns crack and grow in three stages; the wings slam the ground and spread; the three heads roar one after another, then together.
All the same beats, with less time on each.
Option A turns a 6-second change into a moment the player stops and watches, which suits a boss's second phase.
How should the knock-down stun be built?
Three clips: fall, stunned loop, get up

stun_fall (knocked onto its chest), stun_loop (dazed on the ground, heads lolling, breath heaving; loops) and stun_get_up (a heavy, struggling rise). The game decides how long the punish window lasts by how long it plays the loop.
The fall, 3 seconds on the ground, then the rise, all in one clip. Simpler, but the window length is fixed in the animation.
With option A the punish window can be tuned in the game without re-animating.
Hit from the front, hit from the left, hit from the right, and a heavy hit with a bigger recoil. Each lasts 1 second.
Three light variants that differ in which heads and wings recoil.
Front, left and right, each in a light and a heavy version.
Four gives enough variety that repeats are hard to spot, and the left and right variants let the game match the side the player struck from.

wrapup.summary: Version 2 of the goose clips: slower and heavier, a forward death, a longer phase transition, a knock-down stun and separate hit reactions, with version 1 kept for comparison.
wrapup.changing: New version 2 files beside the untouched version 1; the clip script gains a version switch; the rig gains tongue bones only if you pick option A for the tongues.
wrapup.blocking: Nothing is blocked except your answers to the six choices.
